findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Inspector observed multiple areas within the physical facility in need of repair:
1) There is no caulking between the hand washing sink (in front of the office) and the wall.
2) Caulking to the left of the dish machine contains an accumulation of debris, and is fragmented or absent in multiple areas.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple employees change tasks without hand washing. Discussed the need for ongoing education with the staff regarding times to wash hands with the person in charge (PIC). Ensure hands are washed after handling soiled equipment or utensils, after touching cell phones, when switching tasks between handling raw food and ready to eat (RTE) foods, before donning gloves, and after engaging in any tasks that may contaminate the hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a cup being used as a scoop, submerged in sugar. CORRECTED- the PIC removed the scoop with a gloved hand, and placed a scoop with a handle to be used for scooping sugar in a clean plastic bag. Ensure all ready to eat foods are handled with cleaned gloves hands, or utensils that have a clear differentiation between the hand contact surface and food contact surface.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the heat sanitizing dish machine to reach maximum heat plate temperature of 145, after 4+ cycles. Neither wash or rinse temperature gauges on the outside of the machine were moving during the cycle. Inspector directed the facility to use the triple sink to wash-rinse-sanitize all food contact surfaces until the dish machine has been repaired, and observed sanitizing at a minimum temperature of 160F. Inspector will return on 03/02/26 to check for compliance.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.112(A) Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Hot Water Sanitization Temperatures. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, in a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 90°C (194°F), or less than: (1) For a stationary rack, single temperature machine, 74°C (165°F); or (2) For all other machines, 82°C (180°F). [Pf]

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed multiple plates and bowls at the serving station stored with the food contact side upwards. CORRECTED- the plates were inverted after the inspector discussed the need for the food contact surfaces to either be covered or inverted when not actively serving to prevent contamination of the food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted.[C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple food contact and nonfood contact surfaces in disrepair:
1) FIRST REPEAT: Two spatulas hanging in ready to use position on the cook-line were chipped around the perimeter. CORRECTED- spatulas were voluntarily discarded. 
2) The gaskets along the triple door cooler, as well as the warmer (next to the hood system) were frayed or fragmented.
Ensure utensils are checked for integrity to prevent contamination of food. Nonfood contact surfaces should be maintained smooth and easily cleanable. Gaskets should be replaced by the next routine inspection.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple nonfood contact surfaces to contain an accumulation of debris:
1) The condensers of the coffee machines contain an accumulation of soil debris.
2) SECOND REPEAT: The black, (3) segmented container holding ready to use utensils at the island across from the hood contains food debris. 
* Line item #2 was previously noted as violation #44, and has since been moved.
Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed a mop submerged in the basin of the mop bucket. Inspector discussed proper mop storage with the PIC. Ensure mops are stored in a position that allows them to air dry, to prevent the growth of microorganisms.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple areas within the physical facility in need of repair:
1) There is no caulking between the hand washing sink (in front of the office) and the wall.
2) Caulking to the left of the dish machine contains an accumulation of debris, and is fragmented or absent in multiple areas.
3) Coving between the floor and wall is peeling in the chemical storage closet (directly to the right of the entry).
Fixed equipment should be sealed to the wall to prevent the entry and harborage of mold. Ensure physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a sanitizer bucket on the serving line to be at 100 ppm quaternary ammonia. CORRECTED- kitchen staff remade sanitizer bucket to a concentration of 200 ppm. Ensure sanitizer buckets are remade and tested at a frequency to hold the proper concentration- as recommended by the manufacturer's label.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. [P]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspector observed 2 dead insects in a cabinet on the serving line. The PIC is in communication with maintenance- who oversees pest control operations. Inspector will follow up on 09/10/25 to check that the facility has no pests.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions. [C]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple wet sanitizer rags sitting on the counter at the kitchen service counter. CORRECTED- the sanitizer rags were moved into the sanitizer bucket. Ensure wiping cloths are stored in a sanitizer bucket in between uses.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D). [C]

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- Observed clean utensils in the drawers of the island facing the cook line to be stored in black bins which were soiled with food debris. PIC was informed and bins were moved to dish area. Ensure staff are cleaning bins frequently to avoid an accumulation of soil debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination. [C]

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple plates and bowls being stored with the food contact side up, and uncovered. CORRECTED- the PIC inverted the plates and bowls or moved them under coverings. Ensure food contact surfaces are stored under coverings or inverted to prevent contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted.[C[

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed 2 spatulas hanging in ready to use position on the cook-line to be in disrepair. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) voluntarily discarded the two spatulas. Ensure utensils are checked for integrity to prevent contamination of food. Food contact surfaces should be maintained smooth and easily cleanable.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of dirt, wood chips, and insect droppings in a cabinet at the serving line. While there were no items in storage in this cabinet, nonfood contact surfaces in the facility should be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the harborage of pests- see violation #38. A follow up will occur on 09/10/25 to ensure routine cleaning of nonfood contact surfaces is occurring.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a mop submerged in the basin of the mop bucket. CORRECTED- the mop was moved to the top to air dry. Ensure mops are stored in a position that allows them to air dry, to prevent the growth of microorganisms.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Observed clean utensils in the drawers of the island facing the cook line to be stored in black bins which were soiled with food debris. PIC was informed and bins were moved to dish area. Ensure staff are cleaning bins frequently to avoid an accumulation of soil.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed the caulking between the wall and the counter to the left of the dish machine to be molded and damaged. The PIC was informed and will contact maintenance to replace the sealant.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Observed employee drinks stored on the prep table in the kitchen. The prep table was in use to prepare salad. PIC was informed that personal drinks should be stored below prep areas, and the drinks were moved. Ensure staff are storing drinks away from food-contact surfaces to avoid cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.
